|rulings=* If the character is persona replaced by a non-spy version, [[Undercover (Dark){{!}}Undercover]] is lost and the character ceases to be [[Undercover (Dark){{!}}Undercover]].<ref name="scomp">Players Committee, [https://res.starwarsccg.org/rules/SWCCG_2023_AdvancedRulebook.pdf Star Wars CCG Advanced Rulebook] (2023), Appendix C, pp. 173-174, "Undercover Spy Rules" and "Breaking Cover": inactive-state exceptions, prevention of Force drains, deployment without presence or Force icons, loss of spy status, voluntary breaking of cover and loss of undercover-related cards. These are general rules for the undercover state, not a quotation of the original Effect. Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20260422134639/https://res.starwarsccg.org/rules/SWCCG_2023_AdvancedRulebook.pdf Internet Archive] (22 April 2026). Lookup: [https://scomp.starwarsccg.org/?s=Undercover Scomp: Undercover (Dark)].</ref>
* The [[Undercover (Dark){{!}}Undercover]] character prevents the opponent from Force draining at same site, and allows the owner to deploy to same site even without presence or Force icons. These benefits are the same even if the [[Undercover (Dark){{!}}Undercover]] character is a droid.
* The [[Undercover (Dark){{!}}Undercover]] character is inactive (for example it does not participate in battles) but outside of battle it may be targeted by Interrupts and anything that could make it dueled, hit, or lost.
* The owner may voluntarily break cover during their deploy phase.
* If the character's cover is broken (either voluntarily or by another card such as [[Corran Horn]]), then [[Undercover (Dark){{!}}Undercover]] is lost.
